name: Barbell Overhead Press
summary: A foundational compound lift performed by pressing a barbell vertically from the anterior shoulders to full lockout overhead while standing.

setup: Set a barbell in a rack around mid-chest height.
Grip the bar slightly outside shoulder width with a full, pronated grip, keeping the wrists relatively straight.
Step under the bar and rest it across the anterior deltoids and clavicles, with forearms vertical and elbows slightly in front of the bar.
Unrack the barbell, step back into a stable hip-width stance, and squeeze your glutes and core.
steps: Tilt your head slightly back to clear a vertical path for the bar.
Press the barbell straight upward in a tight vertical line.
Once the bar passes your forehead, bring your head and torso forward into a neutral position.
Lock out your elbows overhead with the bar balanced directly over the midfoot, shoulders, and hips.
Lower the barbell under control along the same path, tilting your head back slightly as it passes, and return to the front-rack position.
instructions.breathing: Inhale and brace your abdominals before initiating the press, exhaling past the sticking point near lockout or at the top.
cues: Squeeze glutes and brace your abs.
Push your head through the window at the top.

common_faults.fault: Excessive hyperextension of the lumbar spine to turn the press into an incline press.
common_faults.correction: Squeeze the glutes hard, brace the abdominal wall, and reduce the working load.

common_faults.fault: Pressing the bar forward in a loop around the face.
common_faults.correction: Tilt the head back slightly so the bar can travel in an efficient, straight vertical line.

common_faults.fault: Flaring elbows excessively wide in the rack position.
common_faults.correction: Tuck elbows slightly forward so forearms remain perpendicular to the floor.

precautions: If you miss a repetition, lower the barbell safely back to the anterior shoulders under control; do not drop it behind your neck.
Maintain strict lockout without bending your knees to turn the lift into a push press.
